misconception_notes: All 20 misconceptions converted from the old {check,message,pattern} shape to {pattern,message,expect}. Every expect was derived by committing the specific error and verified distinct from the correct answer (min separation checked, e.g. gold[2] simple-interest 5300 vs compound 5304.50). Errors modelled: dividing by the percent number (bronze[0] 360/25=14.4), stopping at 10% (bronze[1] 25, bronze[2] 8, silver[6] 64), finding the percentage but not adding/subtracting (bronze[3] 20, bronze[4] 18, silver[0] 42, silver[1] 84, silver[4] 9), one-place-only decimal shift (bronze[6] 3.5, bronze[7] 4.5), forgetting the x100 (bronze[5] 0.6, silver[5] 0.4), giving the raw money change not a percentage (silver[2] 5, silver[3] 3000), and reverse-percentage errors (gold[0] adds 15% =586.5, gold[1] subtracts 20% =21600, gold[3] linear 3x10% =14000, gold[4] reverses only one discount =360). No em dashes; all expects reproduce.
opener_concept: Sale-price bar model: a £40 jacket at 25% off, drawn as an inline SVG bar split into four £10 blocks with one shaded as the discount. Boxes: one block = £10 (a quarter of 40), pay £30 after the discount. The reveal names it as finding 25% of an amount (25% = a quarter), then generalises to the multiplier idea (increases add on, decreases take off, reverse undoes the multiply).
completion_boundaries: Every bank walk tags phase:'substitute' after the set-up move (finding 10%/the multiplier/the money change/the combined multiplier), leaving >=2 live boxes for the student to finish and land exactly on the stored solution. Gold reverse walks pre-work the 'what percent is this' step, then the student does the 1%-then-100% finish.
